query: How does the pH scale work?
title: How the pH Scale Works: Acids, Bases, and Hydrogen Ions

scenes.title: The Universal Acidity Scale
scenes.narration: The pH scale measures how acidic or alkaline a chemical solution is, ranging from zero to fourteen.
scenes.key_takeaway: The pH scale spans 0 to 14, measuring chemical acidity and alkalinity.

scenes.title: Hydrogen Ions and the Logarithmic Law
scenes.narration: It quantifies hydrogen ion concentration mathematically as the negative base ten logarithm of proton molarity.
scenes.key_takeaway: pH is inversely proportional to hydrogen ion concentration on a log10 scale.

scenes.title: Logarithmic Multipliers
scenes.narration: Because the scale is logarithmic, each single step represents a tenfold change in hydrogen ion concentration.
scenes.key_takeaway: Each step represents a 10x multiplier in hydrogen ion concentration.

scenes.title: The Equilibrium of Neutrality
scenes.narration: At pH seven, hydrogen and hydroxide balance equally. Lower values are acids, while higher values are bases.
scenes.key_takeaway: pH 7 is perfectly neutral, balancing H+ and OH- ions in water.
